pr_body:
closes #39792

_**PREVIEW BREAKING CHANGES**_
These changes will be breaking from preview 8.

These changes rebrand the customer facing portions of the Diagnostics Server to be called DiagnosticPort.  This is a simpler naming scheme than the previous usage of "forward" and "reverse" servers.

In addition, this solves one major issue of the configuration of DiagnosticPorts.  under the previous configuration knobs, users could only specify 1 "reverse" monitoring agent.  If anyone else attempted to configure a monitoring agent, they would either clobber the user's configuration or be clobbered by the user.  The new configuration knobs allow for multiple diagnostic ports to be configured in a `;` delimited list.

## Nomenclature and Syntax

A `DiagnosticPort` can be configured using the `DOTNET_DiagnosticPorts` environment variable.  The syntax for this configuration is as follows:

```
DOTNET_DiagnosticPorts=<port address>[,tag[...]][;<port address>[,tag[...]][...]]
```

Where:
* `<port address> ::= A NamedPipeName without \\.\pipe\ on Windows | the full path to Unix domain socket on other platforms`
* `tag ::= SUSPEND_MODE | PORT_TYPE`
* `SUSPEND_MODE ::= suspend | nosuspend` (default value is `nosuspend`)
* `PORT_TYPE ::= connect` (future types such as additional `listen` ports could be added to this list)

An example value would be:
```
DOTNET_DiagnosticPorts=$DOTNET_DiagnosticPorts;~/myawesome.sock,connect,nosuspend;/mounted/dir/alternatelonnectablec.sock
```

`DOTNET_DoagnosticPorts` supersedes `DOTNET_DiagnosticMonitorAddress` and `DOTNET_DiagnosticMonitorPauseOnStart` so the latter two have been removed with these changes.

Any Diagnostic Ports specified in this configuration are _in addition to_ the default port, i.e., `dotnet-diagnostic-<pid>-epoch>`.  The suspend mode of the default port is set via the new environment variable `DOTNET_DefaultDotnetPortSuspend` which defaults to `0` for `nosuspend`.

Each port configuration specifies whether it is a `suspend` or `nosuspend` port.  `suspend` induces the PauseOnStart functionality and causes the runtime to halt progress in `EEStartupHelper` before most usbsystems are online.  Since multiple ports can individually request `suspend`, the resume command now needs to be sent **_by each `suspend` port connection_** before the event will be set and the runtime resumes execution.

If a config specifies multiple tag values from a tag type, e.g., `<path>,nosuspend,suspend,suspend`, the **_first_** one is the only one respected.

The `port address` value is required for a port config.  If a config doesn't specify an address and only specifies tags, e.g., `suspend`, then that value will be treated as the path.

The runtime will make a best attempt to generate a port from a port config.  A bad port config won't cause an error state, but could lead to consumed resources, e.g., causing the runtime to continuously poll for a connect port that will never exist.

### additional changes

* fix scoping issue for the runtime identifier GUID used in the process info command and advertise protocol.  Previously, it was marked as a `static` namespace-scoped variable causing each translation unit to get its copy of the variable.  Changing this to `extern` and intializing the value in `DiagnosticServer::Initialize` before use, solves this problem.  Fixes #40696.

* Add `EventPipe::Disable` deferral logic for window of time between resuming the runtime from Pause on Start state to when `EventPipe::FinishInitialization` is called.  A disable in this time frame can cause `EventPipe::StartStreaming` to be called on a session that is in the middle of being disabled.  `EventPipe::Disable` is safe before resuming and after `EventPipe::FinishInitialization`.  `EventPipe::Disable` now checks the `s_CanStartThreads` variable (value is `true` _after_ `FinishInitilization` is complete) under a lock to see whether it can disable or should defer.  The deferred disabled are then safely acted on in `FinishInitialization`

CC @tommcdon @jander-msft @dotnet/dotnet-diag

issue_context.title: Rebrand Diagnostics Server
issue_context.body:
I'll continue to think about the naming. I'm not attached to the specific ones I suggested but I do worry that the term "reversed server" isn't currently planned to show up anywhere else in the overall experience or documentation. I know we have used the phrase internally, but if it shows up in the public facing name I anticipate customers won't find it intuitive. In order to understand 'reversed server' the customer would first need to know what the runtime diagnostic server is and that this term is a derivative from it. I don't think they will know either of those things.

One possibility is that because we haven't spoken much in public or in docs about "diagnostic server" there is probably room to change our planned terminology without causing too much confusion, though the window won't be open much longer. @josalem @shirhatti @wiktork @sywhang if you guys had thoughts?

One thought would be:
```
Runtime env var: DOTNET_MANAGEMENT_PORT=\foo\bar\mysocket
Tool: dotnet-monitor --dotnet-management-port=\foo\bar\mysocket
```
In both contexts I am making port refer by-default to the tool hosted port. If we did this I would stop talking about "Diagnostics Server" and instead say "the runtime has a management port" or "the runtime can connect to a tool's management port." We would also get rid of the current DiagnosticMonitorAddress* environment variables. We could support an optional more generalized syntax for DOTNET_MANAGEMENT_PORT allowing lists of ports, specifying if the runtime should connect or listen, and specifying if the runtime should suspend on start:
DOTNET_MANAGEMENT_PORT=\foo\bar\mysocket,connect,suspend;\baz\socket,listen,nosuspend

_Originally posted by @noahfalk in https://github.com/dotnet/diagnostics/pull/1303#discussion_r455741826_
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

Tagging subscribers to this area: @tommcdon
See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.

I like this idea. Essentially all the plumbing for multiple connections has already been done to enable the reverse scenario. This suggestion would simplify the semantics and make it easier to reason about for customers.

A couple sticky bits come with this though (we discussed some of these offline):

This change would allow different connections to request the suspend features. This would mean that resuming the runtime will become a "stateful" interaction since we would need to know which connection just sent the command and we couldn't resume until all necessary connections have resumed. This is definitely doable, but we'll need to plumb some state through to account for it.
Since this would be using an environment variable with a list, there's the possibility that customers could stomp out some latent configuration. We would need to add some guidance for tool developers and customers that they should set this variable like PATH and only append to it. This is a lot better than the current situation where there can only be one connection specified and if a customer sets it, they may be stomping a latent configuration.
Overall, I think this is all goodness and shouldn't require too much work (famous last words...). My one piece of feedback on this is the naming. Could we use a plural in the env var to hammer in the idea of a list and maybe use address instead of port? address feels a little less specific, while port makes me immediately thing of a TCP port.

_Originally posted by @josalem in https://github.com/dotnet/diagnostics/pull/1303#discussion_r455741826_

> Could we use a plural in the env var to hammer in the idea of a list and maybe use `address` instead of `port`? `address` feels a little less specific, while `port` makes me immediately thing of a TCP port.

The word "port" as a noun is used in other areas of computing beside TCP (especially for physical hardware). In general, it just means some endpoint from which you can access (or provide) information when connected.

If you add support, for example, for getting diagnostics information over TCP ports rather than pipes/domain sockets, would you use the same environment variables? Something like "DOTNET_MANAGEMENT_PORT=tcp:7000,listen,suspend"

What about "DOTNET_DIAGNOSTICS_PORTS" and "--diagnostics-ports" or if you do want to avoid "port" then "DOTNET_DIAGNOSTICS_ADDRESSES" and "--diagnostics-addresses"?

I don't think "management" is a good word to use here because you really don't manage anything with the connection (the runtime isn't being managed by this, the application isn't managed by this, etc; you could argue that one manages the diagnostics state of the runtime, but then it would be named something like DOTNET_DIAGNOSTICS_MANAGEMENT_PORT, and then we're getting into way too lengthy naming territory).

_Originally posted by @jander-msft in https://github.com/dotnet/diagnostics/pull/1303#discussion_r455741826_

> Something like "DOTNET_MANAGEMENT_PORT=tcp:7000,listen,suspend"

Yep!

> What about "DOTNET_DIAGNOSTICS_PORTS" and "--diagnostics-ports"

This is fine by me. A couple nit questions to fully scout the naming:
1. Should it be DOTNET_DIAGNOSTIC_PORTS (removed the 'S' in DIAGNOSTICS)? I can't come up with technical reason why, but pronouncing the two words that end in 's' is harder. Is it just me?
2. I could imagine even if the runtime supports multiple ports that tools are under no obligation to do so. Anyone find it confusing if some places used the singular term 'diagnostic port' and others used the plural 'diagnostic ports'? (I don't)
3. Any concern that --diagnostic-port(s) would conflict with other argument names that dotnet-monitor would be likely to use? What are we calling the two dotnet-monitor endpoints where we are serving http traffic?

> if you do want to avoid "port" then "DOTNET_DIAGNOSTICS_ADDRESSES" and "--diagnostics-addresses"?

Personally I prefer port, partly because it makes it a little easier to use "Diagnostic Port" like a proper noun and know what it refers to and partly because it doesn't clash with other service/proxy terminology that is likely to use 'endpoint' or 'address'.

Not sure if the syntax of the list was fully inferable from my examples but this is a little more fleshed out version of that part:
```
Ports := semicolon separated list of 'Port'
Port := address[,optional_tags]
optional_tags := comma separated list of 'tag'. suspend and nosuspend are mutually exclusive, as are listen and connect.
tag := suspend | nosuspend | listen | connect
```
When specified on the runtime env var 'suspend' and 'connect' are the defaults if not specified in the tags list. When specified in the tool argument 'listen' is the default and 'suspend'/'nosuspend' are ignored entirely if the user writes them. Does this syntax make sense? Its easy to change if there are alternate suggestions : )

_Originally posted by @noahfalk in https://github.com/dotnet/diagnostics/pull/1303#discussion_r455741826_

I've come around on `Port` I think.  It collates the idea of a communication mechanism and a "location" to access the mechanism succinctly and in a recognizable manner to most users.

To your points, Noah:

1. I think `DOTNET_DIAGNOSTIC_PORTS` sounds better as well, but I don't know why.  Part of me wants to be consistent in how we name these things, but this is meant to rebrand the feature so we can do what we want right now 😄 
2. I don't think it would be confusing.  Though I do think we should strive to be consistent, I don't think it should be a sticking point.

I think your syntax works.  I might go one step further and specify that the first tag observed overrules any subsequent tags for mutually exclusive tag sets.  That ensures that we have a non-erroring behavior if someone accidentally over-tags their port.

I think most of the work to support multiple ports like this has already been done, so the remaining work in the runtime would be the following:

- [ ] Add `DOTNET_DIAGNOSTIC_PORTS` config knob
- [ ] Rename `DOTNET_DIAGNOSTICS_MONITOR_PAUSEONSTART` to something that matches this naming scheme specifically for the default port
- [ ] Add logic for consuming Noah's proposed syntax
- [ ] Add logic for multiple connections requesting PauseOnStart (probably the most time consuming part)

Let me know if I missed anything here.  I don't see anything of particular risk.  That being said, I don't think we have a test harness that could stress this right now, so that could be time consuming to build.

> Rename DOTNET_DIAGNOSTICS_MONITOR_PAUSEONSTART to something that matches this naming scheme

Can we get rid of it? The PORTS syntax now includes a per-request setting to suspend so a global mechanism is probably superfuous.

I think you're right, but when I just thought about it, there is one thing we might want to leave it for: using the default port with pause on start.  For example, let's say I want to implement something like `dotnet debug my.dll`.  I could use that variable to turn on the pause on start functionality without needing to create an additional port and then I would just send the resume runtime command via the default port.  Thoughts?

PS: this new terminology is making it much easier to discuss these concepts.
you are right, it could make sense to use that var (or a renamed var) to control the suspension on the default port

> Not sure if the syntax of the list was fully inferable from my examples but this is a little more fleshed out version of that part:
> 
> ```
> Ports := semicolon separated list of 'Port'
> Port := address[,optional_tags]
> optional_tags := comma separated list of 'tag'. suspend and nosuspend are mutually exclusive, as are listen and connect.
> tag := suspend | nosuspend | listen | connect
> ```

The specified syntax implies that when specified on the runtime that the address for the listen mode must be specified, which means that the server endpoint is configurable. As it is today, it is not configurable and is only found at \\.\pipe\dotnet-diagnostic-{pid} or /tmp/dotnet-diagnostics-{pid}-{diambiguator}.

> When specified on the runtime env var 'suspend' and 'connect' are the defaults if not specified in the tags list. When specified in the tool argument 'listen' is the default and 'suspend'/'nosuspend' are ignored entirely if the user writes them. Does this syntax make sense? Its easy to change if there are alternate suggestions : )

When specified on the runtime, shouldn't 'listen' be the default? Or is it that if the DOTNET_DIAGNOSTIC_PORTS env var is specified that it implies that connect mode is the default; the non-existence of this env var is 'listen' and 'nosuspend'?

I think that, given the behavior of of the diagnostic port without the env var, the existence of the env var should assume the same defaults unless otherwise specified. Thus, `DOTNET_DIAGNOSTIC_PORTS='/path/to/port/file'` would be 'listen' and 'nosuspend' by default (if specifying a socket file / named pipe path is allowable for runtimes in listen mode).

Here are my suggested defaults and explicitly laid out syntax combinations:

**Runtime Port (Default Value)**
/tmp/dotnet-diagnostics-{pid}-{diambiguator},listen,nosuspend

**Runtime Port (Name: DOTNET_DIAGNOSTIC_PORTS)**
|Value|Implied|Comments|
|---|---|---|
|{path}|listen,nosuspend|If configuring port path in listen mode is allowed|
|{path},connect|nosuspend||
|{path},connect,nosuspend|||
|{path},connect,suspend|||
|{path},listen|nosuspend|If configuring port path in listen mode is allowed|
|{path},listen,nosuspend||If configuring port path in listen mode is allowed|
|{path},listen,suspend||If configuring port path in listen mode is allowed|
|{path},nosuspend|listen||
|{path},suspend|listen||

**Suggested 'PAUSEONSTART' Rename**
Name: DOTNET_DIAGNOSTIC_PORTS_SUSPEND
Uses the same terminology as the rest of the env vars and values.
I would think setting this env var would override any of the suspend/nosuspend settings for each of the ports in the DOTNET_DIAGNOSTICS_PORTS env var.

**Tool Argument Port (Default Value)**
/tmp/dotnet-diagnostics-{pid}-{diambiguator},connect

**Tool Argument Port (Name: --diagnostic-ports)**
|Value|Implied|Comments|
|---|---|---|
|{path}|connect|If configuring port path in listen mode on runtimes is allowed|
|{path},connect||If configuring port path in listen mode on runtimes is allowed|
|{path},listen|||

The 'suspend' and 'nosuspend' values are not applicable for the tool argument (either failure or just ignored).

> The specified syntax implies that when specified on the runtime that the address for the listen mode must be specified, which means that the server endpoint is configurable. As it is today, it is not configurable and is only found at \.\pipe\dotnet-diagnostic-{pid} or /tmp/dotnet-diagnostics-{pid}-{diambiguator}.

I think something that @noahfalk left out is that this is all _in addition_ to that default listen port.  That would remain regardless of what you specify in this env var.

> Suggested 'PAUSEONSTART' Rename
Name: DOTNET_DIAGNOSTIC_PORTS_SUSPEND
Uses the same terminology as the rest of the env vars and values.
I would think setting this env var would override any of the suspend/nosuspend settings for each of the ports in the DOTNET_DIAGNOSTICS_PORTS env var.

I agree with the name change, however, I don't think this environment variable should force suspend to be on or off for all specified connections.  One of the previous points Noah and I discussed was allowing each connection to specify suspend/nosuspend and have the runtime not resume until _all_ suspend connections send their resume command.  If we make the env var globally set that value, we end up in an unfortunate state where we might be waiting on connections that may never send the resume command.

Otherwise, I agree with the proposed syntax and default implications.  I'll start writing this up today 😃 .
Removing needs-breaking-change-doc-created as that is tracked in #40499
Since this was a new feature in the 5.0 timeframe, wasn't previously documented, and it is only breaking from an earlier preview I'm opting to not do a breaking change document for this issue.

review_comments:
We should probably add a test(s) that ensure the string parsing is robust. Stuff like:
0 length ports, invalid paths, invalid tags, multiple conflicting tags, not setting any tags to use defaults, a path whose name is identical to a tag name
For conflicting tag, the logic will use ~that last~ **_the first_** tag value specified (which should be tested as you're suggesting).  Would expect conflicting or duplicate tags to produce an error?
Added a test that tries various pathological and nonsensical values for the port configs.

The test appears to race the call to StopTracing with the runtime emitting the startup event. Ideally we'd wait on some ManualResetEvent that would be signaled when the startup event is received (or timeout after a while assuming the startup event is never coming and the test should fail).
Added an MRE instead of the bool flag.
